CaseStore.protect seals only registry fields, so it is stored in plain text; the 'exhaustive' control test only checks registry fields, so it passes anyway, and no exception covers this.

Retention.purge now also removes coapplicant_tax_id, and the hold and schedule logic is unchanged. But the only evidence is the sample-coverage RetentionControlTest#sampledPurgeRespectsHold, while RET-1 needs exhaustive evidence and the ledger has no RET-1 entry.

summary: The change adds the co-applicant tax identifier, which is NPI, to the applicant fields without registering it in NpiRegistry or the approved NPI field list. CaseStore therefore stores it in plain text, which violates ENC-1, and no exception covers it. The 'exhaustive' ENC-1 control test passes only because it checks the registry, which omits the new field. The process records (ticket, independent review, control-owner approval, CI on the head commit) are in order, and RET-1 is open because it has only sample-level evidence, but the ENC-1 violation alone requires rejection.
